about: Session usage model of MiSArch (work package C1; WORKLOAD.md). Operation names are the msa model's (misarch-optimization/msa/models/misarch-kotlin.m) until work package A maps them to the extracted GraphQL operations; 'login' is Keycloak's password grant (the Gatling 'Get Access Token'). Times in seconds. Distributions are StoEx strings as SimOxide evaluates them. Step language: {call}, {think} (a named think time), {delay} (a StoEx), {loop, body}, {branch: [{p, body}]}, {use} (a fragment). Generator: workload/gen_sessions.py.

sources.G: MiSArch Gatling scenarios (Ceres experiment-executor templates template_buyProcessScenario.kt and template_abortedBuyProcessScenario.kt; misarch-optimization/02-misarch-experiments-workload.md §2.1): request order, pauses U(4,10) s after the product list, U(0.05,0.15) s between the requests of one page, U(4,7) s after the cart and after the payment data, U(8,12) s before placeOrder.
sources.C: Ceres realistic 30-min run and its 12-h load trace template_realisticUserSteps.csv (02 §2.2, §3.1): 34 % buy / 66 % aborted sessions; arrivals per second have index of dispersion 0.96 (Poisson-like); 60-s windows peak at 1.9 x the mean, 5-min windows at 1.5 x, hours vary by ±15 %.
sources.R2: Round 2 (msa gen_model.py GATLING_RATES, EXTENDED_RATES, KOTLIN_BUY_SHARE = 0.3433; misarch-optimization/calibration/plans/mix_gatling.json): per session one token, products, product, users, address, createShoppingcartItem, and 0.3433 x the four buy requests; assumed rates for operations the load tests never call. Design load 64.2 sessions/s = 0.6 x the measured saturation 107 sessions/s.
sources.TPCW: TPC Benchmark W (TPC-W) specification v1.8, 2002, clause 5 (web interaction mixes): browsing mix 95 % browse / 5 % order interactions, shopping mix 80/20, ordering mix 50/50; think times negative-exponential with mean 7 s (clause 5.3.1.1). Per-page shares as reproduced by Kaszo et al. 2006 (https://conf.uni-obuda.hu/huci2006/43_Kaszo.pdf).
sources.CBMG: D. A. Menasce, V. A. F. Almeida, R. Fonseca, M. A. Mendes: A methodology for workload characterization of e-commerce sites. ACM EC 1999 (customer behaviour model graphs: sessions as probabilistic state machines; customer classes, e.g. occasional vs heavy buyers).
sources.BAY: Baymard Institute: average documented online shopping cart abandonment rate 70.19 % (49 studies, 2023) / 70.22 % (2025), https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate.
sources.VEND: Vendor e-commerce benchmarks (e.g. Littledata, Dynamic Yield, via https://www.smartinsights.com/ecommerce/ecommerce-analytics/typical-average-add-cart-conversion-rates/): about 5-7 % of sessions add to cart, 1.4-3 % convert. Not peer reviewed; used only as an order of magnitude.
sources.BURST: N. Mi, G. Casale, L. Cherkasova, E. Smirni: Injecting realistic burstiness to a traditional client-server benchmark. ICAC 2009, 149-158 (burstiness injected into TPC-W, controlled by the index of dispersion); N. Mi et al.: Burstiness in multi-tier applications: symptoms, causes, and new models. Middleware 2008.
sources.SPIKE: P. Bodik, A. Fox, M. J. Franklin, M. I. Jordan, D. A. Patterson: Characterizing, modeling, and generating workload spikes for stateful services. ACM SoCC 2010 (spikes: a steep volume increase together with a shift of what is requested).
sources.DLIM: J. von Kistowski, N. Herbst, S. Kounev, H. Groenda, C. Stier, S. Lehrig: Modeling and extracting load intensity profiles. ACM TAAS 11(4), 2017 (load intensity = seasonal part + trend + bursts + noise; DLIM/LIMBO, used with Palladio/SimuLizar).
sources.A: Assumption of this package (flagged in WORKLOAD.md).

list.src: G (mean 7 s = TPCW's mean think time)

product.src: A (like a list page; TPCW mean 7 s)

checkout.src: G (buy part of buyProcessScenario); parameters: section cardinalities

cartStart.src: G (product page with user and addresses, then the cart), CBMG (a few product views first), A (registration share)

secondItem.src: A (25 % of cart sessions add a second item)

browser.about: Anonymous window shopper: the product list, then product pages, sometimes back to the list (search/browse). MiSArch serves public products without a token (catalog Query.products: anonymous users see public products), so no login.

cartAbandoner.about: Puts items into the cart and leaves (Gatling abortedBuyProcessScenario, with browsing first).

buyer.about: Puts items into the cart and buys (Gatling buyProcessScenario, with browsing first).

account.about: Returning customer: logs in and does one to three account tasks; the tasks' weights are round 2's assumed rates of these operations.
account.src: R2 (EXTENDED_RATES as weights), A (tasks per session, task sequences)

admin.about: Employee maintaining the catalogue, stock, prices, discounts, taxes and shipment methods; weights are round 2's assumed admin rates. Its own scenario with a constant rate: admin work does not follow the customers' load (R2 scaled it with the load).
admin.src: R2 (EXTENDED_RATES as weights), A (session length, think time, constant rate)

gatling.about: Round 2's workload as one session: the Gatling buy/aborted scenario (buy share 0.3433), then with probability 0.199 one of the operations round 2 added with assumed rates (weights = those rates). Its per-operation rates equal round 2's exactly (gen_sessions.py --check verifies).

gatlingAdmin.about: Round 2's admin operations, one per session, no login, at round 2's assumed rates.

round2.about: Round 2's load as sessions: same operation rates at every load level (validation against the measured system and the round-2 models).

realistic.about: Session classes with a mix per phase; the design load is the number of sessions at which the shopping mix sends as many client requests (logins included, admin excluded) as round 2 at 64.2 sessions/s.

shopping.src: TPCW shopping mix (80/20); buyers / cart sessions = 1/3 (G, C, BAY)

ordering.src: TPCW ordering mix (50/50); a sale converts more of its carts (A: 1/2)

admin.operationsPerSecond: round 2's admin operations at the design load

day.about: A compressed day (DLIM: seasonal part + bursts): a low browsing night, a morning ramp, midday shopping with a short burst (C: 60-s peaks of 1.9 x), a sale spike with the ordering mix (SPIKE: volume and mix change together; BURST), an evening peak, a browsing decline. volume = sessions relative to the realistic workload's design sessions; admin stays constant. The first 120 s warm up and are not measured.

steady.about: The base mix at the design load throughout (stationary comparison with round 2's static evaluation).

login.note: Keycloak password grant (Gatling 'Get Access Token'); not a MiSArch operation

media.uploadMedia.note: msaMapping names media.createMedia, which is not an operation id; the mutation is media.uploadMedia

notifications.note: no round-2 request document; plan by analogy with `address` (root currentUser, User.notifications joined from notification)

registration.note: Keycloak registration; the user service handles Keycloak's user/user/create event (round 2: eventUserCreate)

cardinalities.about: Workload cardinalities that the code leaves open (domain/REPORT.md §9: items per order, coupons, payment methods; the data-dependent accesses: inventory's reservation per item, findApplicableDiscounts per item). '@name' in a call's params refers to these; ${x} to a fragment argument. They become input VariableUsages of the EntryLevelSystemCall.

itemsPerOrder.value: 1 (75 %) or 2 (25 %): the session's cart lines (classes buyer: secondItem branch)

providerSuccess.src: simulation stub default (PAYMENT_SUCCESS_RATE, SHIPMENT_SUCCESS_RATE); a system parameter, not a call parameter

data.about: Data volumes of the measured system (round 2's seed, misarch-optimization/calibration/scripts/seed.py defaults, results-kotlin/seed/state.json). They set rows per access and table sizes; the timing campaign records them per window (timing/CAMPAIGN.md §3.2) and the derivation uses them for rows of list accesses.
